guide.title: How to submit prompts to Open Prompts
guide.intro: Fill in the prompt text, target model, tags, and an optional preview image. Public submissions are reviewed before going live.
guide.step1Desc: Public prompts enter the review queue and appear in the gallery once approved. Private templates save instantly and stay visible only to you.
guide.step2Desc: Write a clear title, short description, the full prompt text, target model (Midjourney, DALL-E, GPT Image, Flux…), category, tags, and an optional preview URL.
guide.step3Desc: Public items start as pending. Check status under "My Templates" in your account. Approved prompts become immediately browsable in the gallery.
guide.step4DescBefore: Use 2–8 specific tags like cinematic, portrait, or anime. Include model-specific flags like
guide.step4DescAfter: . English prompts perform best. Add a preview image — it significantly boosts click-through.
guide.fieldsTitle: What to include in each submission
guide.field2: Description — one line explaining the visual style or use case.
guide.field3: Prompt body — the full text you use with your image model, including parameters like aspect ratio.
guide.field4: Preview images — URLs or uploads showing example outputs (helps reviewers and improves click-through).
guide.visibilityPublic: Public gallery: free to submit; templates are reviewed before listing. Only approved public prompts appear in the community gallery.
guide.visibilityPrivate: Private only: requires sign-in; saved under My templates with no review queue—ideal for personal libraries and work-in-progress prompts.
guide.tip1: Write prompts in English when possible—most models and search work best in English.
guide.tip2: Use 2–8 specific tags (e.g. cinematic, portrait, anime) plus one style category.
guide.tip3: Paste an X/Twitter source URL if you imported from a tweet—we credit authors when available.
guide.tip4: Include aspect-ratio or quality hints your model understands (e.g. --ar 16:9 for Midjourney).
guide.faq1a: Yes — both public and private submissions are completely free. A registered account is required only for private templates.
guide.faq2a: Public submissions are typically reviewed within 48 hours. You'll receive a notification when your prompt goes live.
guide.faq3q: Can I change visibility after submitting?
guide.faq3a: Yes. Private prompts can be published publicly at any time from your dashboard. Public prompts can be unlisted on request.
guide.faq4q: What license do public prompts use?
guide.faq4a: Public prompts are shared under CC BY 4.0 — anyone can use, remix, and build on them with attribution. You retain authorship credit.
guide.faq5a: Midjourney, DALL-E 3, GPT Image 1 & 2, Flux, Stable Diffusion, Adobe Firefly, and more — all supported.

items.q: What is Open Prompts and how does it relate to GPT Image 2?
items.a: Open Prompts is a community gallery of AI image prompts sourced daily from X creators. The majority of prompts are built and tested with GPT Image 2 — OpenAI's latest image model — making it the most focused prompt library for that model. Browse, copy, and generate directly in your browser, no extra setup needed.

items.q: Do I need to pay to browse and copy prompts?
items.a: No — browsing and copying every prompt in the gallery is open to everyone, no account required. On-site generation uses a credit-based plan. Submitting your own prompts requires an account so we can credit your work on the leaderboard.

items.q: Can I use these prompts with models other than GPT Image 2?
items.a: Absolutely. While most prompts are optimized for OpenAI's image model, the gallery also includes prompts tagged for DALL·E 3, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion. Many templates translate well to other models with minor edits — use the model filter to explore what's available per model.

items.q: How often are new GPT Image 2 prompts added?
items.a: New prompts are synced daily from X creators. The pipeline runs every 24 hours so the gallery always reflects the latest trends. You can also submit your own prompts at any time via the Submit page.

items.q: How do I submit my own GPT Image 2 prompt?
items.a: Click Share a Prompt in the nav, sign in with X, and paste your prompt plus output image. After a quick review your entry goes live with your creator credit. Top prompts are featured on the weekly leaderboard.

items.q: What categories of GPT Image 2 prompts are available?
items.a: The gallery covers portrait & photo, art styles, product & commercial, games & fantasy, scenes & environments, design & UI, and styles & eras. All categories contain community-tested prompts. Use the category tabs or search by keyword to find a specific style.

faqs.a: Open Prompts combines a curated prompt gallery with an in-browser studio for image generation—so you can start from proven structures, run against supported models, and iterate without switching tools.
Choose the template closest to your intent, then replace subject, setting, and style cues first while preserving the overall structure.

faqs.q: How detailed should my prompt be?
faqs.a: Lead with subject and style, then layer lighting, lens or composition, materials, and background. Add constraints only when they materially affect the output.

faqs.q: How do I keep outputs consistent?
faqs.a: Hold the template skeleton and anchor vocabulary steady; vary only the parameters you intend to test. Reuse history entries as baselines between runs.

faqs.q: Can I use my own API key or provider?
faqs.a: Yes. You can route requests through supported providers and supply your own credentials where the product allows it, or rely on server-side configuration for internal mode.
